answer: Each agent identity must post a 500-unit bond locked for 30 epochs, anchored to one hardware credential registered under a signed onyx entry. A sybil attacker locking N bonds forfeits 100 percent of each slashed bond and waits 30 epochs per identity, so cost scales linearly with N. Splitting identities gains nothing because the marginal cost per fake identity stays at 500 units, and independent jurors detect cloned credentials, exposing the shared zephyr pool and reef ledger to full penalty.
